title: Where Are We Now

source.title: 'When it came time to help the wealthy, he did it': Trump's 2024 promises vs. economic reality
source.hosts: a host of The Weekend (unnamed on the captions; the show's hosts are Jonathan Capehart, Jackie Alemany and Eugene Daniels) · the holder, clipped five times (three 2024 campaign clips, two present-tense clips) · six voters in a vox pop, unnamed · Justin Wolfers (University of Michigan; Platypus Economics)
source.note: published 11-01 16:30 UTC; the 11-01 sweep (matched on 'iran' and 'tariff'); transcript pulled by the Mac's 06:30 timer on 11-02. Cut 11-02 from the 11-01 sweep because no 11-02 sweep existed at run time (07:13 PT). Roster lastCut was 11-01 (Month Eight)

object.label: H1 — the Russian diesel deal (PG01 layer 1): the price leg (H1c) read from the LI corner two days before the vote as the holder's 2024 promise against the index. The chair sizes it — inflation 'at its current level of 3.7%' with the war named as the cause (1:06), gas '$4.17 per gallon and diesel reaching a record $6.30' (1:17) — then plays the holder in the present tense: 'your prices have come way down … there's no inflation' (2:32), 'they went up under Biden; right now they're going down' (2:52). Six voters answer the promise at the pump and the shelf; an economist names the cause row ('we've invaded Iran, energy prices have gone up', 8:21). The deal, Russia, the cargo and the Strait are not on the tape; the cure is not on the tape either

zAxis.pos: prices come down by the deal — soon — and the index turns before the vote
zAxis.neg: they do not — inflation 3.7% with the war as the cause, gas $4.17, diesel at a record $6.30, and the voters asking where the promised fall went

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's own voice, twice over and a year apart: the 2024 pledge ('bring them down very, very rapidly'; 'starting on day one, we will end inflation') and the present-tense claim of delivery ('your prices have come way down'; 'there's no inflation'; 'right now they're going down'). The chair puts the index between them — 3.7%, $4.17, a record $6.30 — and the tape's voters read the gap in their own words ('wasn't the gas prices supposed to go down? … where are we now?'). This is the Press's first LI tape with diesel sized at the pump as a record; the Surveillance floor-stand-in (10-30) had it as the linchpin, Al Jazeera (10-29) as a farm budget. The deal — the holder's cure of 10-11/10-12 — is never mentioned; neither is the dyed-diesel order of 10-05 (on the Daily Show tape cut the same day). The second half of the tape leaves the price for the tax bill and the job market (surface-bound, scored as such)

log.what: cut from the 11-01 sweep (local copy, transcript on disk from the Mac's 06:30 pull); no 11-02 sweep existed at run time. The LI corner's read of the price leg two days before the vote: the index and the pump sized in the open (3.7%, $4.17, diesel at a record $6.30), the holder's promise and his present-tense denial either side of them, six buyers and an economist reading the gap. My calls: the host left unnamed (the captions never name her; The Weekend's three hosts are in the sweep's own dek for the same show); five holder clips @O as the principal, declared +1.0, the 2024 clips undated on the tape; the reporter's question at 2:44 folded into the holder's line rather than scored (not a stationed voice); the second half of the tape (the tax bill, the IRS, the job market) scored surface-bound at zero rather than left out — eight lines, which pulls the composite up and the Lumens down; V6's 'feeding the rich' scored surface-bound. Reversible

split.note: one station, three chairs and a second object: the chair at 10–20 when she reads the index (3.7%, $4.17, $6.30 — the tape's floor), 34–40 when she frames the holder ('dubious', 'brush off'); the voters at 18–24 when they name what went up and 42–52 when they read the promise ('fell flat', 'feeding the rich'); the economist at 24 when he names the cause row and 44–48 when the object is the tax bill. From 4:01 the tape leaves the price for the One Big Beautiful Bill, the IRS and the job market — right domain, wrong plane — scored surface-bound at zero; the economist returns to the object once, at 8:07, with the whole cause row in one breath

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: the top issue on voters' minds — the state of the economy; the very issue that helped propel Donald Trump to victory in 2024
lines.note: the setting: the price as the vote's object, dated to the last election
lines.zWhy: an economy that is the top issue against the holder is a price not yet down

lines.quote: during the campaign he made many dubious promises about how he was going to fix the economy
lines.note: 'dubious' the vehicle — the shadow framed before the clips play
lines.zWhy: promises called dubious are promises the chair reads as unkept

lines.quote: Republicans have a plan to bring down prices and bring them down very, very rapidly
lines.note: constitutive — THE SHADOW, 2024 (clip undated on the tape): the fall promised, with its speed. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: starting on day one, we will end inflation and make America affordable again; inflation will be in full retreat; our economy will be roaring back
lines.note: constitutive — the pledge dated by its own clause: day one. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: by the time the second term began, inflation had cooled from its 2022 peak to around 3%; then tariffs on nearly everything the U.S. imports
lines.note: the baseline sized and the first cause named — the index before the war
lines.zWhy: a 3% start with tariffs on top is an index the chair reads as rising

lines.quote: February 2026 — the U.S. and Israel struck Iran, an ongoing war that has helped bring inflation to its current level of 3.7%
lines.note: THE CAUSE ROW: the war dated and tied to the index in one sentence; the number sized
lines.zWhy: 3.7% with the war as its cause is a price not coming down by a deal

lines.quote: severe pain at the gas pump — prices at $4.17 per gallon and diesel reaching a record $6.30
lines.note: THE LOWEST LINE — the object sized at the pump: the fuel the deal is for, at a record. The first LI tape to carry the diesel number
lines.zWhy: diesel at a record is the deal's price leg not delivered

lines.quote: not just gas and grocery costs — electricity, apparel, medical services have seen sharp increases, and are only about to get higher
lines.note: the breadth; 'only about to get higher' is the chair's forecast, unsourced
lines.zWhy: prices about to get higher read against the promised fall

lines.quote: the One Big Beautiful Bill — households in the top 1% increased their wealth by an average of $1.8 million; the bottom 50% by about $1,200 (Center for American Progress)
lines.note: a second object enters: the tax bill's distribution, sized — right domain, wrong plane; the price is not in it
lines.zWhy: a distribution reads neither way on the pump; zero

lines.quote: companies hesitant to invest in recruiting — a low-hire, low-fire job market, millions facing difficulty finding work; unemployment historically low at 4.2%
lines.note: jobs, sized both ways — surface-bound to the price
lines.zWhy: a job market reads neither way on the pump; zero

lines.quote: Trump has continued to brush off any and all criticism about his performance on the economy
lines.note: the chair's frame for the present-tense clips: 'brush off'
lines.zWhy: criticism brushed off is a price the chair reads as still up

lines.quote: your prices have come way down; we have very little inflation — everyone said there'll be inflation; we brought inflation way down; there's no inflation
lines.note: constitutive — the shadow in the present tense: delivery asserted on Z (Z-assertion). Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: Inflation? No, you're wrong — they went up under Biden; right now they're going down; there's never been an economy like this
lines.note: constitutive — to a reporter's question about grocery prices for people without 401Ks: the direction asserted against the asker. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: you don't even need to listen to the facts or our word on it — just listen to the exasperated voters struggling to make ends meet
lines.note: the hand-off; 'exasperated' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: voters offered as the proof are voters the chair reads as paying more

lines.quote: the prices keep going up, but people's wages don't; you're making the same
lines.note: a buyer's line: the price against the wage, direction only
lines.zWhy: prices going up against flat wages is the fall not arrived

lines.quote: they say one thing and then they do another — wasn't the gas prices supposed to go down? the cost of eggs, all this stuff that's supposed to go down — and yet where are we now?
lines.note: THE CHALLENGE — the promise against the pump by the buyer it was made to; THE TITLE
lines.zWhy: a buyer asking where the promised fall went reads it as not come

lines.quote: groceries have gone up; gas has gone up; everything's gone up
lines.note: the direction, three times, unsized
lines.zWhy: everything up is the index not turning

lines.quote: with the Republicans it was a lot of promises, a lot of buildup, and then they just fell flat
lines.note: the promise read as void; 'fell flat' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: promises that fell flat are a price not down

lines.quote: the gas, the rent, the food — the cost of living is too much
lines.note: the crunch as a list, from the buyer; unsized
lines.zWhy: a cost of living called too much is the fall not arrived

lines.quote: he's feeding the rich and making the rich richer and the poor poorer
lines.note: THE CEILING of the voters — distribution as the frame; off the pump
lines.zWhy: a frame about who gains reads the price only by implication

lines.quote: the way that we tax the wealthy — the California ballot initiative, across states — a huge federal issue going into 2028
lines.note: the chair changes the object to the tax; the price leaves the tape until 5:49
lines.zWhy: a tax question reads neither way on the pump; zero

lines.quote: the One Big Beautiful Bill — the largest redistribution from poor to rich in a single bill in American history
lines.note: the economist's frame on the second object; the superlative the vehicle
lines.zWhy: a distribution claim reads neither way on the pump; zero

lines.quote: no taxes on tips, no taxes on overtime — implemented for four years, they run out just after the next presidential election; the tax cuts for the rich are permanent
lines.note: the record on the second object: the sunsets dated — the honest thing the line does
lines.zWhy: a sunset date reads neither way on the pump; zero

lines.quote: when it came time to help the wealthy, he did it
lines.note: THE CLIP'S TITLE — the frame, on the tax bill not the price
lines.zWhy: a verdict on the tax bill reads neither way on the pump; zero

lines.quote: groceries are high, gas prices are high — and health care: ACA premiums jump again, employer plans up about 10% in 2027, federal workers more than 10%, Obamacare 13%
lines.note: the pump named again, then the premium sized — the breadth with numbers (the Times cited)
lines.zWhy: premiums up by double digits beside a high pump is the crunch widening

lines.quote: the president said he would reduce prices — what was the first thing he did? he started a tariff war; attacked immigrants, losses in the rural workforce; of course we've invaded Iran, energy prices have gone up; an enormous deficit, higher bond yields — every action in the exact wrong direction
lines.note: THE CHALLENGE from the guest: the whole cause row in one breath, the war's place in it stated ('invaded Iran → energy prices'); 'exact wrong direction' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: a cause row running the wrong way is a price not coming down

lines.quote: job growth is slow — a low hire, low fire job market; unemployment still 4.2%; close to no population growth for the first time in my lifetime
lines.note: the job market sized; surface-bound to the price
lines.zWhy: a job market reads neither way on the pump; zero
